model: County-run Medical Assistance Transportation Program (MATP). Of 67 counties: 38 use a county vendor, 13 a DHS direct agreement, 8 a county sole service provider, 7 a hybrid, and 1 a DHS broker (Philadelphia, since 2005).
managed_care_members: Not carved into managed care: MATP is run by the member's county, and plans help coordinate. Community HealthChoices plans pay for emergency ambulance and some non-emergency ambulance and stretcher trips; nursing facilities transport their own residents.
broker_or_vendor: Philadelphia: Modivcare (formerly LogistiCare), paid a capitated per-member-per-month rate. Other counties use local transit agencies or vendors; Dauphin County moved MATP to rabbittransit on July 1, 2026.
contract_term: Philadelphia contract dates not published. The pending solicitation (RFA 06-24) offers 3 years plus one 2-year option.
procurement_status: RFA 06-24 for Philadelphia (issued Jan. 2025) is stayed while litigation is pending; two earlier solicitations were cancelled after bid protests. A statewide broker solicitation was cancelled in 2019 after the legislature stopped it.
legislation_and_studies: Act 46 of 2025 required a study of a statewide broker. The June 2026 study found the risks significantly outweighed the benefits and described ongoing work to improve the county model instead: updated MATP standards, PennDOT review of policy changes, and a Find My Ride module for mileage reimbursement requests. It put SFY 2025 spending at about $133.5 million for 4.1 million trips, about $32.65 per trip.
oversight_and_performance: No 2025–26 statewide audit found. Counties monitor their own programs.
oversight_agency: Department of Human Services, Office of Medical Assistance Programs; counties.

model: One broker statewide, under two regional contracts (Downstate: New York City, Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester and Putnam; Upstate: the rest of the state).
managed_care_members: Carved out of managed care. Managed long-term care plans stopped arranging rides on March 1, 2024, and the broker took them over; the broker also took over rides for Fidelis members in Rockland County on April 1, 2026.
broker_or_vendor: Medical Answering Services (MAS), which took over Long Island from Modivcare on Dec. 1, 2023.
contract_term: Two five-year contracts, Aug. 1, 2022 to July 31, 2027. Renewal options not found.
procurement_status: The 2021 RFP allowed one statewide broker or two regions. Modivcare protested the award to MAS; the State Comptroller denied the protest on May 30, 2023. A rebid ahead of July 2027 was not found.
legislation_and_studies: S4862 and A7329 would remove the requirement in Social Services Law § 365-h that brokers manage Medicaid transportation; both were re-referred to the Health committees on Jan. 7, 2026. A May 2025 policy limits covered rides to opioid treatment and outpatient programs to the member's local medical market area.
oversight_and_performance: LeadingAge NY has raised cancellations and wheelchair and stretcher access with the Department of Health and the broker (as reported).
oversight_agency: Department of Health; State Comptroller approves contracts and decides protests.

model: One statewide broker. State rules require that all non-emergency medical transportation be provided through an independent transportation broker (N.J.A.C. 10:50-1.4).
managed_care_members: Carved out of NJ FamilyCare managed care; plans remain responsible for emergency ground and air transport.
broker_or_vendor: Modivcare (formerly LogistiCare), first awarded the contract effective July 1, 2009.
contract_term: Contract T2503 began Sept. 1, 2017 and has been extended by change order, most recently through Feb. 27, 2027. The term of the rebid contract was not found.
procurement_status: Rebid (bid 24DPP01040) drew quotes from three bidders by March 4, 2026. A notice of intent to award to MTM (Aug. 6, 2026) was protested; on Aug. 20, 2026 the Division of Purchase and Property found MTM's quote non-responsive, cancelled the notice, and remanded the matter for award to Modivcare as the only remaining responsive bidder. The decision could be appealed to the Appellate Division within 45 days; that period ended in early October 2026, and no appeal had been reported as of Oct. 20, 2026. No final award had been posted as of that date.
legislation_and_studies: A985 (introduced Jan. 13, 2026) would set broker vehicle, staffing and performance standards and require reports to the Department of Human Services; a similar 2024 bill, A5032, did not advance past committee.
oversight_and_performance: The most recent audit found is from 2016: HHS-OIG found inadequate oversight and $64.7 million in noncompliant claims. No 2025–26 performance reports found.
oversight_agency: Department of Human Services, Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services; Treasury's Division of Purchase and Property runs the procurement.

model: Two regional transit authorities serve as brokers statewide, under contracts with the Executive Office of Health and Human Services (EOHHS) Human Service Transportation (HST) Office, which arranges rides for six state agencies, including MassHealth.
managed_care_members: Brokered rides cover MassHealth Standard, CommonHealth and CarePlus members. One Care, Senior Care Options and PACE plans coordinate their members' rides. How ACO and MCO members are handled could not be confirmed from a current source.
broker_or_vendor: Montachusett Regional Transit Authority (MART) for western, central, Metro Boston and northeastern Massachusetts; Greater Attleboro-Taunton Regional Transit Authority (GATRA) for the southeast, Cape Cod and the Islands. Brokers are paid at cost for transportation, with a shared-ride incentive, plus a fixed monthly management fee.
contract_term: Start and end dates not published. A 2022 broker procurement consolidated nine service areas into three.
procurement_status: No current or upcoming broker procurement found.
legislation_and_studies: No NEMT-specific legislation or budget action found. From Jan. 1, 2026, members who lost Senior Care Options eligibility book rides through the HST brokers.
oversight_and_performance: A May 8, 2025 State Auditor report on FY21–FY23, when MassHealth paid the two brokers $283.3 million, estimated at least $1.67 million in overpayments for rides on days with no qualifying medical service.
oversight_agency: EOHHS Human Service Transportation Office and MassHealth; State Auditor.

model: One statewide broker for HUSKY Health (Medicaid) and Covered CT members.
managed_care_members: Statewide broker covers HUSKY A, C and D and Covered CT, according to the 2023 RFP.
contract_term: The 2023 RFP set full operation from Oct. 1, 2024, a base term to Sept. 30, 2027, two one-year extensions at the agency's discretion, and a $200.35 million cap. An executed contract confirming these terms was not found.
procurement_status: RFP issued Oct. 16, 2023; proposals due Dec. 4, 2023. No next rebid found.
legislation_and_studies: HB 5356 (2026) would require the Department of Social Services to review NEMT rates at least annually and would let drivers with a pending taxi or livery license endorsement provide NEMT for up to 90 days; it cleared Human Services 21–2 and was tabled for the House calendar on April 7, 2026. A 2025 bill with a similar driver provision, SB 1298, cleared committee 22–0; final action not found.
oversight_and_performance: The legislature's Medicaid oversight council reviews broker performance. In June 2025, on-time performance was reported above 90% in most months, against a 90% target, and a participant raised hospital discharge delays of 12 to 15 hours.
oversight_agency: Department of Social Services; Council on Medical Assistance Program Oversight.
